deals.evidence: Pera decided he would buy Kaplan's 14-percent stake in the team and the 14-percent stake Straus owned instead of selling his 25-percent stake.
deals.headline: Pera buys out minority owners Kaplan and Straus under buy-sell clause
deals.summary: Kaplan and Straus triggered the buy-sell agreement in fall 2017; Pera chose to buy their 14% stakes each rather than sell his 25%. The price was not disclosed.

name: Memphis Grizzlies
notes: Revenue, operating income, player expenses and gate receipts are Forbes estimates for 2024-25 (calculated October 2025); Forbes' page gives no team owner or purchase price. Deal stake_pct 28 is Kaplan's 14% plus Straus's 14% as SI states each; SI gives Pera's own stake at the time as 25%. Pera's current percentage is not stated. Josh Kushner's former minority stake (ESPN: 'previously was a minority owner of the Memphis Grizzlies'; reported by Forbes in March 2019 at a $1.32bn valuation, but that Forbes page returned 403) has no readable date/stake, so it is not a deal row. Shirt sponsor Robinhood is from Forbes' Heat page (2024-25). NBA.com's feed gives FedExForum capacity 18,119; Forbes says 17,794. Not found: chief executive, legal entity, attendance, social counts, any institutional holder.

owners.evidence: When Pera bought the team in 2012, his group paid $377 million, according to Tillery.
owners.name: Robert Pera

ownership_summary: Controlled by Robert Pera (founder of Ubiquiti), whose group bought the team from Michael Heisley in 2012 for $377 million. In 2018 Pera kept control by buying out minority owners Steve Kaplan and Daniel Straus (14% each) under a buy-sell clause. Josh Kushner was previously a minority owner.
